source.title: Attractor cortical neurodynamics, schizophrenia, and depression

confidence_rationale: Directly substantiates MECH-450's psychiatric_failure_mode dimension: in recurrent attractor networks, too-weak excitation/inhibition makes high-activity (winner) states unstable -> failure to hold a selection (avolition/negative-symptom analog), while reduced inhibition makes the network jump to attractor states without adequate input -> spurious commitment, and over-connected/over-stable attractors -> rigid non-reward fixation (depression). These map onto MECH-450's two failure poles (indecision vs locked attractor) with high fidelity. Confidence held below 0.8 because it is a conceptual review and the disorders are cortical (PFC/OFC) attractor analogs, not the BG selection step per se.
failure_signatures: Reduced firing rates / reduced recurrent excitation (e.g. NMDA hypofunction) destabilize the high-activity winner attractor -> the selection cannot be held = MECH-450's too-weak-settling indecision/abulia pole.
Reduced inhibition lets the network make a noise-induced jump to a high-firing attractor even without adequate input -> a committed selection that is not warranted by the evidence (spurious winner).

An over-connected, over-stable attractor (e.g. the OFC non-reward system in depression) cannot be flipped by new input -> the perseveration / locked-attractor pole MECH-450 predicts for runaway recurrent gain.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Cortical recurrent-collateral attractor networks underlie memory, attention and decision-making; their stability is set by recurrent excitation (NMDA) and inhibition (GABA). Reduced excitation/firing destabilizes high-activity attractor states (negative/cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia); reduced inhibition causes noise-induced jumps into attractor states without external input (positive symptoms); and an over-connected, over-sensitive non-reward attractor network in the lateral orbitofrontal cortex underlies depression.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-450 predicts two breakage poles for a recurrent settling competition: too-few/too-weak inhibition rounds -> failure to converge to a single winner (indecision/abulia), and runaway recurrent gain -> a locked attractor that new evidence cannot flip (perseveration/obsessional fixity). Rolls supplies the mechanistic neuroscience for both poles plus a third (reduced inhibition -> unwarranted spontaneous commitment), grounding the claim's psychiatric_failure_mode section in an established attractor-instability framework.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rolls's attractor networks are cortical (PFC short-term memory, OFC reward/non-reward), not the basal-ganglia committed-action selection step MECH-450 models; the failure-mode mapping is by shared dynamical class (recurrent attractor stability), not by shared anatomy. Whether the V3 fixed-inhibition settling step actually exhibits these poles is an empirical question the eventual REE ablation must test.
mapping.source_context: Conceptual/computational review linking attractor-network stability parameters to schizophrenia and depression symptom clusters in humans.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative review by a foundational attractor-dynamics theorist (source_quality good). Mapping_fidelity high for the failure-mode dimension specifically; the claim's psychiatric_failure_mode text reads almost as a restatement of Rolls's stability poles. Transfer risk moderate: cortical attractor -> BG selection step is a shared-dynamics analogy, and the human-disorder mapping is itself a model, not a measurement of the REE substrate.
